newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH TRADE MINISTER SAYS NO NEED FOR CROWN DEVAL.
newsitem.headline: CZECH TRADE MINISTER SAYS NO NEED FOR CROWN DEVAL.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy on Monday said there was no need to devalue the crown in order to curb ballooning current account and trade deficits but the situation should be monitored closely.

When asked at a news conference whether, in his view, the current situation -- a record 100.9 billion crown trade deficit and a current account shortfall of $1.7 billion -- called for a change to the exchange rate Dlouhy said:
"The current situation does not require it. (But) the current account deficit is approaching the point where it is necessary to observe it quite closely."
The Czech trade deficit hit 100.9 billion crowns for the first eight months of the year, compared to a 59.5 billion crown deficit for the same period in 1995.
The Czech Statistical Bureau has forecast the current account deficit to rise to 81 billion crowns, or 5.7 pct of GDP, in 1996.
So far, the trade deficit has not translated into significant pressure on the Czech crown which is being supported by large inflows of short term capital.
Many analysts have cautioned that a devaluation may be needed in order to keep Czech exports competitively-priced.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus had called a meeting with his three top economic ministers, central bank governor Josef Tosovsky, and CSU director Edvard Outrata had been called for October 8 to address the situation.
But on Monday Dlouhy said the meeting had been postponed because of a parliamentary session, which could include discussion of the budget. No new date for the meeting has been set.

In September, Dlouhy said the trade deficit could reach crisis proportions in 1997 if current trend continues and called for domestic wage restraint and company restructuring to boost competitiveness.

On Monday, he added that the spiralling deficit was partly attributable to the economic slowdown in the European Union (EU). "If the rate of growth of exports to the Euroepan Union had been the same this year as last year, the deficit would be around 25 billion crowns lower," he said.
